_comment: Nuclear fleet policy & licensing database for Step 12 retirement analysis. CfD-style policy support: payments fill the gap between market revenue and a guaranteed floor, they do NOT stack on top of profitable operations. 45U and state programs do NOT double-stack — whichever provides the higher effective floor applies.
_sources: NRC ADAMS (license dates), EIA-860 (capacity), state PUC filings (ZEC/CMC/PPA terms), IRA legislative text (45U)

45U_PTC.name: Federal 45U Nuclear Production Tax Credit (IRA)
45U_PTC.mechanism: CfD: pays max(0, $15/MWh − (energy_rev + capacity_rev)/MWh). Phases out when grid avg wholesale price exceeds threshold. Does NOT stack with state programs — plant receives whichever CfD floor is higher.
45U_PTC.notes: IRA Section 45U. Sunsets after 2032. Political uncertainty around extension given IRA rollback pressure.

IL_CEJA_CMC.name: Illinois CEJA Carbon Mitigation Credits
IL_CEJA_CMC.mechanism: CfD: ICC sets indexed price floor. If market revenue (energy + capacity) exceeds floor, plant pays back the difference. Floor > 45U floor, so CMC dominates when active.
IL_CEJA_CMC.notes: Replaced IL ZEC program. Floor of $33.38/MWh indexed to CPI. Expiry mid-2027. Renewal depends on IL General Assembly. Political support moderate — strong clean energy constituency but affordability pressure.

NY_ZEC.name: New York Zero Emission Credits
NY_ZEC.mechanism: CfD: NYSERDA purchases ZECs at fixed price minus social cost of carbon adjustment. Effective floor ~$17.48/MWh (2025 tranche). Plants receive payment only if merchant revenue is below floor.
NY_ZEC.notes: Extended through Tier 4 CESPR to 2029. Strong NY political support for nuclear as CES backstop. Expected to transition into CES Tier 1 eligibility post-2029.

NJ_ZEC.name: New Jersey Zero Emission Credits
NJ_ZEC.mechanism: CfD: BPU set ZEC price at ~$10/MWh for 3-year terms. Program expired June 2025 — not renewed.
NJ_ZEC.notes: Expired. PSEG and Constellation now fully merchant for NJ nuclear fleet. BPU signaled no renewal interest.

cfd_stacking_rules.rule: Plants receive the HIGHER of (45U floor, state policy floor) — they do NOT stack. If market revenue already exceeds the applicable floor, no CfD payment is made.
cfd_stacking_rules.example: A plant earning $40/MWh from energy+capacity in IL (CMC floor $33.38): no CfD payment needed. Same plant earning $28/MWh: receives $5.38/MWh CfD top-up to reach $33.38 floor.
cfd_stacking_rules.post_expiry: When a policy expires, the plant falls back to the next-highest floor (e.g., IL CMC expires 2027 → falls to 45U $15/MWh floor through 2032 → fully merchant after 2032).
